correctness.rationale: Identify J(n,2)−{ab} with line graph of K_n−ab. A selected edge set F is total dominating exactly if every selected edge has an adjacent selected edge (no component K2) and the set of isolated original labels is empty, one vertex, or exactly {a,b}; any other pair of isolates would produce an undominated edge. All graphs without K1/K2 components on j labels have polynomial h_j=j![x^j] exp(−x−zx²/2)∑_{l≥0}(1+z)^C(l,2)x^l/l!. For the undeleted graph, T_n=h_n+n h_(n−1); by edge symmetry, the weighted sets containing a fixed edge ab have generating polynomial z T_n'/C(n,2). Removing those and adding exactly two isolated labels a,b gives the stated P_n. For s chosen edges, c nontrivial components and q≥0 cycle rank, incident labels r=s+c−q ≤s+floor(s/2); with ≥n−2 active labels this yields ceil(2(n−2)/3). Equality forces acyclic component profiles of P3s and one or two four/five-vertex trees depending on n mod3; Cayley tree counts and labelled partitions give explicit M_n. Independent exhaustive direct edge-subset checks n=4..7 yielded total counts 24,436,15286,1022190 and min-set counts 8,3,16,635, agreeing with the exact recurrence. Analytic generating-functions/forest proof is essential for all n.
residual_risks: Finite checks are not universal proofs.

final_claim: For every n≥4, deleting a single vertex from triangular graph J(n,2) yields the full total-domination polynomial P_n(z)=T_n(z)−zT_n'(z)/C(n,2)+h_{n−2}(z), with h_j the no-K1/no-K2 labelled graph polynomial; the exact minimum is ceil(2(n−2)/3), and all minimum selected-edge forests and their labelled counts are classified in three residue classes modulo 3.
limitations: Exactly one J(n,2) vertex removed and n≥4; nothing asserted for multiple deletions or J(n,k) k≥3.
